correctness.rationale: The vertex triples span the sum-one hyperplane and their Gaussian score covariance equals 3 on-diagonal, minus one within each edge and plus/minus one across incident edges, exactly five plus and four minus per graph wedge. A translated bivariate Gaussian density integral proves the \(N^{-3/2}(\log N)^{-1/4}\) dependent exceedance estimate. With O(N+Omega) neighboring signed pairs, the existing local-dependence Poisson process theorem implies independent positive and negative exceedance Poisson limits under Omega=o(m^{3/2}(log m)^{1/4}). Since the Gaussian projection radius is chi_d, its normalized error is negligible. A linear-size edge matching under uniform degree bound supplies tail integrability, proving the stated moment formulas. The 231-point covariance and 840 width checks executed; simulations are not used to justify the infinite conclusions.

value.rationale: The natural graph two-star count controls a quantitatively defined Euclidean angular invariant of canonical graph polytopes. Universality simultaneously covers bounded-degree paths and cycles and dense complete graphs, whereas the known star case has a different half-normal fluctuation mechanism. The five-plus/four-minus incidence covariance census and the density-vs-hub threshold explain a structural geometric distinction; the bounded-degree constant for the vanishing width variance is precise and nontrivial. This is not a generic relabeling or an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
